text: Welcome to This is My Architecture. I'm Rebecca Choi, Solutions Architect from AWS. Together
with me today we've got Michael Leach who is the Enterprise Architect of Malco Resorts and
Entertainment. Welcome Michael. So please tell us a bit about what does Malco do? Okay so Malco is
an owner, operator and developer of entertainment and casino resort facilities. I've heard that
you've developed an application for Malco customers called Malco Club. Will you please
share a bit on that application? Okay so yeah we've developed an application for our customers.
It gives them a personal and holistic interaction with our brand. We have it in two different variants.
One is a WeChat variant which is popular for our mainland China market and we also have it in a
standard iOS or Android application which is predominantly for our international market.
Right so what does the high-level solutions architecture look like? So at a high level
we went with a serverless architecture. It involves services such as API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB
along with other key third-party services. Right okay so what's the rationale behind of choosing serverless architecture?

So Malco Club is a new application we wanted to get up and running as quick as possible. So it was fast to start and we didn't have to provision a whole bunch of infrastructure and support that infrastructure.
The other reason was that we wanted dynamic scaling. So we wanted the architecture to respond to the customer demand.
Right so let's double click into the solution design. Would you please show us the application flow?
Sure so we have our iOS or Android application Malco Club and our WeChat mobile app. They both call an endpoint at API Gateway.
So once the request has made it to API Gateway, the authorizer service which is hosted in Lambda is invoked for member related services.
Right yeah.
So once the service is invoked, the token is decoded and checked or validated against our other systems.
Right so after the user request is authorized, where does the request go?
So once the request has been authorized, it will continue to the relevant Lambda service.
So one of these services could be hotel reservations, could be dining reservations or payments.
Right so where do you choose to put your persistent data?
So we store our data in DynamoDB. So if a function requires access to that data, it will call the DynamoDB endpoint.
Is there any particular reason of choosing DynamoDB?
Yeah so we wanted a database solution that was fully managed so that we didn't have to focus on performance tuning and other maintenance activities.
We also quite like the fact that DynamoDB has individual table scaling.
Right so you also mentioned that the Malco Club applications contains of different functions like hotel reservations, dining, booking.
What is the architecture approach you've taken to deploy those services onto the Lambda?
So we went with a common microservices approach.
We separated these key functionalities into different capabilities.
So in practical terms, we deployed separate Lambda functions for each separate capability.
So this gives us the ability for the architecture to scale independently.
Right it also gives you the flexibility of having different release cycles of different functions as well.
Yeah that's right. So based on our business requirements, we can change our release cycle.
Hotel bookings may require a release sooner than the dining reservations service.
Right that's great. So there is also a need for the Macro Club applications to integrate with third parties.
How do you secure the API between the Lambda functions and third parties API?
Yeah so most of our third parties have a SOAP or a REST API.
So Lambda will call our APIs directly.
So in line to the request, Secrets Manager is called to obtain the credentials for the third party.
We chose Secrets Manager because we can manage the whole lifecycle of our credentials.
Right. I think it also gives you the benefits of not necessary to hard coding the Secrets in your applications, right?
Yeah that's right. So it's more secure.
Yeah. So that's great. So thanks for sharing the details.
Is there any plan to further optimize the solutions architecture?
Yeah. So we're looking at EKS, the managed Kubernetes service from AWS.
That will give us the ability to deploy more complex services.
And also we can remove some of the constraints around the Lambda functionality for processing time or memory constraints.
